correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly constructs iid packet labels for an a=2^k GSR shuffle, localizes correct guesses to the first/last packets except on a Chernoff-exponentially small event, and exactly reduces packet hits to occupation of {-a,...,-1} by a centered span-one geometric-increment random walk. The uniform Fourier local limit and ordered-visit moment expansion, with a Dirichlet integral and moment determinacy, establish the half-normal limits and every fixed moment. Separate packet halves yield independent copies and the Gaussian rotation yields the CDF and variance. The packaged standard-library checker passes 86 exact rational marginal comparisons and 3806 pathwise/finite numerical checks. Assumptions and normalization have been verified, with no reliance on finite simulation as proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary full text, Section 6, explicitly leaves the score distribution for k≥2 open after proving the fixed-k optimum and its mean. The new distributional law uses joint a-packet labels and independent geometric occupation counts, not derivable from one-position marginals or the earlier fixed-k expectation alone. The known 2024 one-riffle limit is credited as the k=1 boundary. A highly related published published-finding corpus RESULT.md was read in full: it optimizes the expected score when every card is guessed exactly once, with a different optimum and without a score distribution. No exact or stronger covering claim arose in actual searches; residual historical equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: An older equivalent result phrased as a renewal occupation limit for repeated-guess riffle scores could have escaped title/semantic searches.
Not all historical card-guessing and random-walk papers were examined in full; the 2024 and 2025 related sources were compared using accessible material and the 2026 full-text discussion.
No independent expert priority or mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The 2026 primary paper identifies the fixed-k≥2 distribution as an outstanding next problem: its expected value and optimal strategy do not determine higher moments. This result supplies the entire nondegenerate probability law, all fixed moments, the sharp variance coefficient and a transparent independent-boundary-local-time mechanism for arbitrary fixed shuffle count. It is a natural central statistic for this established game and has direct dependence-level significance beyond the known leading mean.
